title: Cock-a-Leekie Soup
subtitle: Scottish chicken and leek broth
excerpt: Cock-a-leekie is one of Scotland's oldest and most comforting soups. Chicken thighs simmer with leeks, carrot, and celery in a well-seasoned broth until tender. Prunes are traditional but have been left out here for simplicity.
sourceNotes: Based on Scottish cock-a-leekie tradition. The soup dates back several centuries and is a staple of Scottish home cooking. Prunes are often added in the traditional recipe for sweetness.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead. The broth deepens in flavour overnight.

content.text: Traditional recipes often include prunes, which add sweetness and body to the broth. They have been left out here, but feel free to add 8 stoned prunes with the leeks in step 3 if you like. The leeks should be washed well between their layers before slicing, as they hold grit.

items.prepNote: washed well and sliced into 2cm rounds

content.text: Put the chicken thighs, stock, carrot, celery, bay leaves, and thyme into the stockpot. Bring to a boil.
Skim any foam from the surface. Reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 20 minutes. Add the leeks. Continue simmering for 20 more minutes.
Lift the chicken out. Pull the meat into shreds using two forks. Return the shredded chicken to the pot.
Remove the bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Season the broth generously. Serve in deep bowls with chopped parsley.

items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes to reduce and concentrate.
Add leeks only in the last 20 minutes of cooking.
Season well at the end and use a good-quality stock.
